remarks: This is a retry of the same state/service. Net result: NO IMPROVEMENT in verified-source count (still 2 verified, same two DGFASLI sources as before). Every *.jk.gov.in host (singlewindow.jk.gov.in, law.jk.gov.in, rgp.jk.gov.in, jk.gov.in) still fails identically with a TLS-layer connection reset, reproduced on repeated retries spaced several seconds apart this session, exactly as in the prior attempt.

The agent-proxy status endpoint's recentRelayFailures log shows this is NOT specific to J&K or to this task: at the time of this retry, the same 'ws_closed_mid_exchange' tunnel failure was simultaneously hitting many unrelated Indian state-government hosts (e.g. labour.ap.gov.in, swcs.rajasthan.gov.in, fabkerala.gov.in, industries.assam.gov.in, kswift.kerala.gov.in, cglabour.gov.in, apindustries.gov.in, labour.rajasthan.gov.in, pblabour.gov.in, labour.kerala.gov.in), and the same 'connect_unreachable' 502 pattern was hitting other unrelated hosts (rpcb.rajasthan.gov.in, egazette.rajasthan.gov.in, bip.rajasthan.gov.in, invest.rajasthan.gov.in, industries.kerala.gov.in). This looks like a broad, session-wide egress/network condition affecting many Indian .gov.in-family domains right now, not a J&K-specific or URL-specific problem that more retries would fix.

One genuinely new and noteworthy finding from this retry: investjk.in, which previously only produced an opaque proxy 502, now completes its TLS handshake and returns a real HTTP 301 redirecting to https://rajasthanssoidlogin.in — an unrelated non-government domain unreachable itself. This suggests investjk.in's DNS/hosting may have lapsed or been reassigned and it may no longer be the legitimate J&K Invest Promotion & Facilitation Cell site at all. This is a substantive finding worth flagging to whoever maintains this source list, independent of this session's network limitations, though it does not add a verified source.

labour.gov.in also changed failure mode (reset -> HTTP 200) but remains unusable: it is a client-side-rendered Next.js shell with no server-side text, so it still fails the spec's 'not an empty JS shell' check regardless of network reachability.

nsws.gov.in was re-fetched and again returns only a generic authenticated-profile shell; it does list Jammu and Kashmir among all states in a generic navigation menu, which is a marginal confirmation that J&K is onboarded to NSWS in principle, but still no J&K- or factory-license-specific content is visible without login, so it remains excluded per the same reasoning as before.

Conclusion for this retry: network conditions for the *.jk.gov.in domain family and services.india.gov.in are unchanged from the prior attempt (still fully blocked), so the verified list is not better in count. The investjk.in finding is new information but points toward exclusion, not inclusion. No padding was added to verifiedSources to manufacture an improvement; the list stays at the same 2 genuinely verified sources as the original compilation.
